clips.title: Introduction to GitHub Actions - Part 6 - Repository Rulesets
clips.why: You see a ruleset that requires a workflow to pass, and a pull request that cannot merge until it does, which is how plugin-ci / validate guards our plugin repository.
look: The required status check is named by the workflow's job, so renaming the job breaks the rule.
A failing check blocks the merge button, even for the repository's owner when no bypass is set.
clips.after: Our plugin repository requires plugin-ci / validate and allows no bypass for agent apps, so a missing version bump cannot reach main.

clips.title: Lessons From a CI/CD Supply Chain Attack at Grafana Labs
clips.why: A real incident where a small change to automation ran code with more power than anyone noticed, which is the reason our risk job marks hooks, scripts and MCP servers for a careful look.
look: How the attack started: code from a pull request ran in a place that had access it should not have had.
Nobody saw it in review, because the change did not look dangerous as text.
clips.after: A plugin hook runs on every laptop and agent machine, so plugin CI labels such a change and asks the reviewer to run it, not only read it.

practice.q: Make validate fail the CI job on warnings too.
practice.why: Without it, validate passes with warnings, and a hook under an unknown event would merge and be ignored on every machine.

practice.q: Which change does NOT get the high-risk label?

options.text: A new sentence in the body of plan-and-grill's SKILL.md
options.why: Body text is read by Claude, not run. Evals judge whether it helps.

options.text: A new server entry in a plugin's .mcp.json
options.why: An MCP server is a program that starts with every session that has the plugin.
A hook runs as a command on every matching event, on every machine.

practice.q: Put plugin CI's jobs for one pull request in the order they can run.
items: Install the pinned Claude Code version
claude plugin validate --strict on the catalogs and every plugin
The skills check and the version check
The eval cases of each changed plugin, with and without the plugin
practice.why: The cheap checks that need no model come first; the evals only run when the plugin is valid and versioned.

practice.q: rhino-core is at 0.4.0 on main, and your pull request fixes one line in its verify skill. Write a version that makes the version check pass.
practice.hint: Anything higher than 0.4.0; a small fix usually raises the last number.
practice.why: The check only asks for a higher version. A small fix raises the patch number, the last one.
